signals_spec.len_tokens: Total token count of the query.
signals_spec.short_query: Alias for len_tokens; low values favor svm/bm25.
signals_spec.has_temporal_cue: True if the query contains explicit temporal markers (e.g., today, yesterday, last week, 2024, 09:30).
signals_spec.update_verbs: True if verbs like now/changed/switch/updated/still/anymore appear.
signals_spec.num_digits: Number of digit characters in the query.
signals_spec.proper_noun: True if capitalized proper nouns detected.
signals_spec.quote_like: True if quoted or code‑like string detected (e.g., "ACME-42").
signals_spec.idf_like_high: Crude rarity proxy: >=2 tokens look rare (length>=6 or mixed case/symbols).
signals_spec.idf_like_low: Crude commonness proxy: many very short tokens (<=3 chars).
signals_spec.paraphrase_synonym_hint: True if query hints at similarity/description/summary wording.

decision_rubric: Else if quote_like OR num_digits>=1 OR idf_like_high -> bm25
Else if paraphrase_synonym_hint OR idf_like_low -> faiss
tie_breakers: If multiple rules match AND has_temporal_cue true, prefer time_weighted.
If short_query<=4 AND quote_like true, prefer bm25 over svm.
If both lexical and semantic signals present, prefer faiss for paraphrase‑heavy queries.
If long query (len_tokens>=12) with no strong signals, prefer tfidf.
anti_patterns: Do not write anything outside the required JSON.
Do not choose time_weighted without a genuine temporal/recency need.
Do not pick svm for long queries unless other signals say otherwise.
output_schema: Return exactly two keys: {"retriever": <one of allowed_values>, "CoT reasoning": "<= 18 words"}
